A-05.decision: Owner-approved reconstruction exception (T-007, Issue I-002). The raw and canonical source value stays 44.94; this is an inferred override, not a source correction, and applies to no other anchor.
evidence: Propagation from the surrounding anchors independently predicts about 49.95 degrees.
49.94 degrees preserves trajectory and angular-momentum continuity with neighbouring anchors.
Contemporaneous PAO trajectory readouts after docking (GET 3:46 and 4:04) agree materially better with the 49.94 degree trajectory.
44.94 degrees creates large unexplained residuals into neighbouring anchors.

T-014 searched the NASA post-launch mission report, the technical air-to-ground and PAO transcripts, the Apollo Flight Journal docking transcript, and NASA-CR-108349. No independent full CSM state vector or BET near GET 3:24 was found. PAO reported scalar speed/range at GET 3:46 and 4:04; these are not a complete state. The 44.94-degree source value remains documentary-unconfirmed, so this 49.94-degree exception remains inferred with status and confidence unchanged.

Propagated with Earth J2, Moon and Sun, A-33 at 4 075.0 ft/s grazes entry (125 km perigee near GET 195:06), consistent with Table 7-VI's shallow -0.70 deg entry predicted after TEI; at 4 375.0 it misses Earth by about 970 km.

A-34.decision: Owner-approved reconstruction exception (T-010, Issue I-006, 2026-10-06). The raw transcription stays "4 374.0" ft/s; this is an inferred override, not a source correction. Printed and reconstruction values are in km/s (ft/s x 0.0003048). Reconstruction value 4 074.0 ft/s.
evidence: The hundreds digit of the Table 7-II p. 7-9 velocity cell is illegible on the NTRS scan; the transcription read it as 3.
Propagated with Earth J2, Moon and Sun, A-34 at 4 074.0 ft/s meets A-35 within 38 km / 56 m/s (print rounding 39 km); at 4 374.0 it misses by 37,893 km / 10,831 m/s with no burn in between.
At 4 074.0 ft/s A-34 reaches entry interface at GET 195:03:08.6, 3.18 S 171.97 E, -6.48 deg, against Table 7-VI after MCC-5: 195:03:08, 3.17 S 171.99 E, -6.46 deg.
A burn of 4.8 ft/s (Table 7-VI) separates A-33 and A-34, so their speeds should differ by about 1 ft/s, as 4 075.0 and 4 074.0 do.
